questions.q: What did Yahweh say the sacrifices produced for him?
questions.a: Yahweh said the sacrifices produced a pleasing scent for him.

questions.q: What two animals, one in the morning and one in the evening, were to be offered in the regular burnt offerings each day?
questions.a: The sacrifices in the regular burnt offerings in the mornings and in the evenings were to be male lambs without blemish.

questions.q: What else did they have to offer with the regular burnt offering?
questions.a: They had to offer a tenth of an ephah of flour as a grain offering mixed with a fourth of a hin of beaten oil.

questions.q: Where was the regular burnt offering first established?
questions.a: It was first established at Mount Sinai.

questions.q: What was the drink offering to Yahweh that had to be added to those regular burnt offerings and what did they do with it?
questions.a: One fourth of a hin of strong drink had to be added to these sacrifices and poured out in the holy place.

questions.q: What had to be offered on the Sabbath day?
questions.a: On the Sabbath day, two male lambs, each a year old without blemish and flour mixed with oil, and a drink offering had to be offered.

questions.q: What special animal sacrifices had to be made at the beginning of each month?
questions.a: At the beginning of the month the animals of the special sacrifices were two young bulls, one ram, and seven one year old male lambs without blemish.

questions.q: What were the grain offerings given with the two bulls and for the one ram?
questions.a: The grain offering for each of the two bulls was three tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil, and the grain offering for the one ram was two tenths of fine flour mixed with oil.

questions.q: What was the grain offering for each male lamb?
questions.a: Each male lamb had a grain offering of a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil.

questions.q: How often were these special burnt offerings to be given?
questions.a: These special burnt offerings were to be given every month throughout the year.

questions.q: What was offered with the regular burnt offering and the drink offering?
questions.a: One male goat was offered as a purifying sacrifice to Yahweh.

questions.q: On what day was the festival to be held and what kind of bread was eaten for seven days?
questions.a: The festival was to be held on the fifteenth day of the first month, and they ate bread without yeast for seven days.

questions.q: When did Yahweh’s Passover come?
questions.a: Yahweh’s Passover came during the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month.

questions.q: What did they on the first day of the Passover, and what did they not do that day?
questions.a: They had a holy assembly and on that day they did no regular work.

questions.q: What animal sacrifices had to be made during the seven days of the Passover?
questions.a: They offered two young bulls, one ram, and seven one year old male lambs that were healthy.

questions.q: What grain offerings did they give with the two young bulls and with the ram?
questions.a: With the bulls they offered three tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil and with the ram they offered two tenths.

questions.q: What did they offer with the lambs?
questions.a: With each lamb they offered a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil.

questions.q: Why was the male goat given?
questions.a: The male goat was given as a purifying sacrifice to make atonement for the Israelites.

questions.q: What were the festival offerings in addition to?
questions.a: They were in addition to the regular burnt offering of the morning.

questions.q: How many days were these offerings to be given during the festival?
questions.a: They were to be given every day for seven days, besides the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.

questions.q: What happened on the seventh day of the festival of the Passover?
questions.a: On the seventh day of the festival of the Passover they had to have a holy assembly and do no regular work on that day.

questions.q: What animal sacrifices had to be made on the day of the firstfruits?
questions.a: They had to offer two young bulls, one ram, and seven one year old male lambs.

questions.q: What did they have to offer on the day of the first fruits, and what did they do on that day?
questions.a: On the day of the first fruits, they offered a new grain offering to Yahweh, and had a holy assembly and did no regular work on that day.

questions.q: What grain offerings did they give with the bulls and the ram on the day of the firstfruits?
questions.a: With each bull they offered three tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil, and with the ram they offered two tenths.

questions.q: What did they offer with the lambs on the day of the firstfruits?
questions.a: With each lamb they offered a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil.

questions.q: What was offered to make atonement on the day of the firstfruits?
questions.a: One male goat was offered to make atonement for the Israelites.

questions.q: What were the offerings in addition to, and what condition did the animals have to meet?
questions.a: They were in addition to the regular burnt offering and its grain and drink offerings, and the animals had to be healthy.

commentary.text: The offering on the sabbath and new moons.
Offerings at the passover, and on the day of first-fruits.

Verses 1–8 God saw fit now to repeat the law of sacrifices. This was a new generation of men; and they were concerned to keep their peace with God when at war with their enemies. The daily sacrifice is called a continual burnt-offering; when we are bid to pray always, at least every morning and evening we should offer up solemn prayers and praises to God. Nothing is added here but that the wine poured out in the drink-offering is to be strong wine, to teach us to serve God with the best we have. It was a figure of the blood of Christ, the memorial of which is still left to the church in wine; and of the blood of the martyrs, which was poured out as a drink-offering on the sacrifice and service of our faith, Php 2:17.

Every sabbath day, beside the two lambs offered for the daily burnt-offering, there must be two more offered. This teaches us to double our devotions on sabbath days, for so the duty of the day requires. The sabbath rest is to be observed, in order more closely to apply ourselves to the sabbath work, which ought to fill up the sabbath time. The offerings in the new moons showed thankfulness for the renewing of earthly blessings: when we rejoice in the gifts of providence, we must make the sacrifice of Christ, that great gift of special grace, the fountain and spring-head of our joy. And the worship performed in the new moons is made typical of gospel solemnities, Isa 66:23. As the moon borrows light from the sun, and is renewed by its influences; so the church borrows her light from Jesus Christ, who is the Sun of righteousness, renewing the state of the church, especially under the gospel. (Nu 28:16-31)

By the sacrifices enjoined in this chapter, we are reminded of the continued power of the sacrifice of Christ, and of our continual need to depend thereon. No hurrying employments, or perilous situations, or prosperous circumstances, should cause slackness in our religious exercises; but should rather stir us up to greater diligence in seeking help from, or giving thanks to the Lord. And all is to be accompanied with repentance, faith is the Lord Jesus, and love to him, and to produce true holiness in our conduct towards all men; otherwise God will abhor our most solemn services and abundant devotions. And Christ is able to supply the wants of every day, every week, every month, every year, every ordinance, every case.
